note.title: Case and grammar role
note.overview: This note supports 7 source-backed questions on Case and grammar role.
learningGoals: Identify the grammatical clue and apply it accurately.
mustMemoriseRules: The nominative servus is the subject.
The nominative canis is the subject.
The accusative canem receives the action.
The dative fratri means “to the brother”.
ad takes the accusative for movement towards.
The dative servo means “to the slave”.
non directly negates tacet.

note.subject: latin
note.title: Declension recognition
note.overview: This note supports 5 source-backed questions on Declension recognition.
learningGoals: Identify the grammatical clue and apply it accurately.
mustMemoriseRules: Usually feminine; nominative often ends in -a.
Often masculine in -us/-er, neuter in -um.
Nominative varies; use genitive to find the stem.
Less common at this stage.
Rare at this level; dies is the key example.

workedExamples.task: Which typical genitive singular ending identifies the 1st declension?
workedExamples.stimulus: epistula, epistulae; porta, portae; terra, terrae
workedExamples.why: Usually feminine; nominative often ends in -a.

workedExamples.task: Which typical genitive singular ending identifies the 2nd declension?
workedExamples.stimulus: servus, servi; liber, libri; templum, templi
workedExamples.why: Often masculine in -us/-er, neuter in -um.

workedExamples.task: Which typical genitive singular ending identifies the 3rd declension?
workedExamples.stimulus: civis, civis; frater, fratris; homo, hominis; pax, pacis
workedExamples.why: Nominative varies; use genitive to find the stem.

workedExamples.task: Which typical genitive singular ending identifies the 4th declension?
workedExamples.why: Less common at this stage.

workedExamples.task: Which typical genitive singular ending identifies the 5th declension?
workedExamples.why: Rare at this level; dies is the key example.

commonMistakes: Recognising the meaning but submitting an incomplete form or spelling.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the required direction.
Recall the form before looking at the options.
Check spelling, ending, case, person and tense before submitting.
